body.statement: For every \(e=(j,h)\in\mathcal E\) and \(w\in\mathcal F_s\), \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,K,p}}|a_e(w)^{\top}m|=b_e(w)=L\lVert x_j-\sum_iw_{jh,i}x_i\rVert_2+\delta\). Each endpoint is attainable for that coordinate by a member of the model class.
body.justification: Exact support functions prevent the upper band from hiding an assumed or loose bias bound.
body.gap: ArmstrongKolesar2018 gives convex-class worst-case bias for scalar affine estimators; the displayed radius exploits the staggered donor simplex and cellwise misspecification class.
body.consumer: The formula lets \texttt{augsynth::multisynth} report the marginal price of predictor imbalance and declared misspecification for each horizon.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(e=(j,h)\), put \(t=T_j+h\), and define the predictor discrepancy
\[
d_e(w)=x_j-\sum_iw_{jh,i}x_i.
\]
By \texttt{ass:mean-structure} and the definition of \(a_e(w)\),
\[
a_e(w)^{\top}m
=d_e(w)^{\top}\beta_t+r_{jt}-\sum_iw_{jh,i}r_{it}.
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz, \texttt{ass:coefficient-radius}, \texttt{ass:cellwise-misspecification}, and the simplex identities \(w_{jh,i}\geq0\) and \(\sum_iw_{jh,i}=1\) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\left|a_e(w)^{\top}m\right|
&\leq \lVert d_e(w)\rVert_2\lVert\beta_t\rVert_2
   +|r_{jt}|+\sum_iw_{jh,i}|r_{it}|\\
&\leq L\lVert d_e(w)\rVert_2+\frac\delta2
   +\frac\delta2\sum_iw_{jh,i}\\
&=L\lVert d_e(w)\rVert_2+\delta=b_e(w).
\end{aligned}
\]
It remains to prove that this support-function bound is exact.  If \(d_e(w)\neq0\), set
\[
\beta_t=L\frac{d_e(w)}{\lVert d_e(w)\rVert_2};
\]
if \(d_e(w)=0\), set \(\beta_t=0\).  Set \(r_{jt}=\delta/2\) and \(r_{it}=-\delta/2\) for every donor with positive weight.  The focal cell is distinct from every donor cell because \(T_j\leq t<T_i\) for a donor \(i\), so these assignments are consistent.  Set all remaining coefficient and remainder coordinates to zero and define \(m\) by \texttt{ass:mean-structure}.  These choices satisfy the two radius assumptions and give
\[
a_e(w)^{\top}m=L\lVert d_e(w)\rVert_2+\delta=b_e(w).
\]
Negating the displayed choices of \(\beta_t\) and \(r\) gives \(a_e(w)^{\top}m=-b_e(w)\).  Each choice extends to a member of \(\mathcal M_{N,T,K,p}\): take \(Q\sim N(m,\Sigma_Q)\), choose arbitrary treated potential outcomes, and define observed outcomes by \texttt{ass:consistency}; the fixed covariance already obeys the covariance-band requirement.  Hence both endpoints are attainable and the supremum of the absolute bias is exactly \(b_e(w)\).
